title: post-pager quickrun and followups
content:
Context:
- Night pager woke at 03:38 UTC for increased 5xx rate on hosted-api route /v1/generate. Alerts triggered by burst of grpc timeouts from gpu-pool-7.
- Mitigations applied: rotated traffic to standby pool, restarted inference-worker on gpu-pool-7 nodes, bumped autoscaler min to avoid cold starts for next hour.

Timeline (quick):
- 03:36 - first grpc timeout alert (obs service).
- 03:38 - Pager. Checked metrics -> connection reset / deadline-exceeded spikes across 3 pods on gpu-pool-7.
- 03:42 - Exec restart of inference-worker on node gpu-pool-7-a (kube cordon + drain -> uncordon).
- 03:49 - Traffic gradually recovered after fallback routing; 5xx rate returned to baseline by 03:56.

Immediate hypotheses (what looked most likely):
1) NTP/time drift on some hosts causing grpc/ssl handshake failures (we've seen similar transient timeouts before).
2) Underlying NVLink/kernel bug after a patch during last maintenance window causing intermittent RPC failures.
3) A spike in prefix-cached misses combined with a small batch-size causing OOM/eviction cascade (less likely: OOMs not present in logs).

Commands I used / checkpoints for follow-up debugging: (copy-pasta for next oncall)
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-infer -l pool=gpu-pool-7 -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl logs -n redwood-infer <pod> -c inference-worker --since=15m | egrep "deadline|timeout|grpc|handshake"
- ssh gpu-pool-7-a 'timedatectl status; journalctl -u inference-worker --since "1 hour ago" | tail -n 200'
- (if kernel suspicion) sudo dmesg | egrep "GPU|nvlink|oom|kill"

Runbook TODOs (short, actionable):
- Add a quick time-sync healthcheck to infra-prober: endpoint that fails if ntp offset > 1s. (owner: Mina) [JIRA-5142, priority: P2]
- Add an alert that combines grpc deadline-exceeded with node-level kernel messages (reduce noisy single-pod alerts). (owner: Liam)
- Update fallback routing doc with explicit steps to increase standby pool weights (include exact kubectl patch commands). (owner: Avery)

Handoff notes for next oncall (bullet):
- If you see grpc deadline spikes from a single pool, immediately route 30–50% traffic to standby first (pattern: route by pool tag, not by node).
- Avoid full drain+restart on more than one node in the same rack at once; caused cluster pressure in past incidents.
- Check /ops/maintenance log for any kernel/driver upgrades in last 48h.

Open questions / investigation items (can be deferred to next day):
- Is there an uptick in time skew across hosts correlated with last week's package update?
- Any kernel oops or GPU driver messages in the nodes that recovered slower? (collect /var/log/messages and send to infra-research)
- Should we widen the autoscaler cooldown for gpu pools to avoid thrash during short transient spikes?

Personal quick checklist before logging out: (done)
- posted brief incident note in #incident-ops (yes)
- linked logs to JIRA-5142 (yes)
- left annotated pod logs in /tmp/postpager-avery-031928 (yes)

Small ideas for long-term resilience (brain-dump):
- implement per-pool connection pooler in front of workers to smooth client retries and avoid flapping during node restarts.
- automated canary of time sync after orchestrator updates (post-maintenance smoke).

Anything else:
- If you pick up this ticket tomorrow, start by grepping for "deadline-exceeded" across the last 24h for all gpu pools and paste top-5 offending pod IDs into the JIRA comment.

-- Avery
